General Motors (GM) is one of the world's leading automotive manufacturers with iconic vehicle brands like Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac. We’ve been shaping the future of driving since 1908: building trusted vehicles, pioneering technologies, and delivering innovation at scale. With our unmatched breadth and expanding portfolio, we’re creating the one for every drive and working toward a future with zero crashes, zero tailpipe emissions, and zero congestion.

A GM vehicle isn’t just a car—it’s the one that’s right for you. With over a century of design and engineering excellence, GM creates vehicles that fit real lives and real journeys. Our vehicles combine groundbreaking innovation with intuitive features to deliver unmatched safety and enduring quality. It’s not just built to drive; it’s built for excellence.

General Motors (GM) was founded on September 16, 1908, in Flint, Michigan by William Durant. GM has a rich heritage and has been shaping the automotive industry with transformative innovations for over a century. Grounded in Alfred Sloan’s vision of creating “a car for every purse and purpose,” GM continues to enable choice for consumers with a broad range of vehicles for every journey.

GM makes vehicles across four brands — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac. GM’s portfolio includes retail vehicles for people’s everyday lives, commercial vehicles to support businesses, and performance vehicles for winning on the race track. GM offers electric vehicles (EV), internal combustion engines (ICE), and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS).

GM is headquartered in Detroit, Michigan, and operates over 150 U.S. facilities including assembly plants, tech centers, distribution hubs, and offices.

GM’s culture is inclusive, collaborative, and driven by purpose. With 20+ teams across design, engineering, software and more, our employees are shaping the innovations that move people and connect them to what matters most. We’re building a future with zero crashes, zero tailpipe emissions, and zero congestion —and we need bold thinkers to help get us there. If you’re ready to make a real impact, explore careers at GM.

https://www.gm.com/company/about-us.raw_html:
About us

Finding the one starts right here

A portfolio of excellence

More than 90,000 employees driving global impact. 150+ facilities sparking progress for communities and economies across America. Four iconic vehicle brands providing the one for every drive.

We’ve set the standard for over a century — and yet, we’re only getting started. That’s the commitment it takes to drive the world forward for years to come.

In a lane of our own

What does it take? Everything.

A passion for engineering. A curiosity to design for what’s next. The determination to continue growing, with decades of expertise and innovation behind us. At GM, this is what we deliver across our portfolio of vehicles—all so that you can find the one for you.

Obsession with the craft

We design incredible cars with an attention to detail that’s second to none. Our vehicles are perfectly engineered for your journey.

American drive

We’re here to win. It’s why we’re committed to being a leader in every lane — from creating jobs and growing the economy to solving for safer roads and cleaner energy.

Life-changing technology

The 1st electric starter. The 1st telematics system. One of today’s most advanced assisted driving systems. Since day 1, we’ve been solving for what matters.

Time-tested strength

We have 100 years of expertise and resilience behind us. Our legacy gives us the perspective to continue creating reliable, quality, and iconic vehicles — and today, we’re stronger than ever.

Our latest wins

Cadillac LYRIQ: German Luxury Car of the Year (2025)

America's Most Awarded Brand for New Vehicle Quality (J.D. Power, 2022-2024)1

#1 in Total Domestic Vehicle Sales (2024)2

#2 in Total Domestic EV Sales (2025)3

Our latest launch

2026 Cadillac VISTIQ

With the Cadillac VISTIQ, moments of luxury are a daily expectation. This all-electric SUV turns heads with modern interiors and colors, captivating choreographed exterior lighting, and available 23" wheels.

Learn more See the full EV portfolio

Careers

Drive the world forward

Design the future of driving. Solve the industry’s toughest challenges. Wherever you find your spark, join us and make a difference.

Start your journey at GM

General Motors (GM) sets itself apart with deep design and engineering expertise, iconic brands, and a clear vision for the future. For over a century, we’ve built vehicles that people trust. Today, we continue to push the industry forward, creating the one for every drive and leading the way toward a world with zero crashes, zero emissions, and zero congestion.

At General Motors, we’re driven by a passion to create the one for every purpose and journey. Since 1908, we’ve been continually advancing the automotive industry, raising the bar for excellence with every innovation and moving people forward. Today, we’re working toward a future with zero crashes, zero emissions, and zero congestion—for every driver, every purpose, and every road ahead.

GM has pioneered major innovations that have shaped both the auto industry and modern life — from the first assembly line and the first PCV valve to commercial room air conditioning and extended-range electric vehicles. During the COVID-19 pandemic, GM produced 30,000 ventilators to support frontline efforts, reflecting a deep commitment to bringing the best of our innovation to our communities.

GM’s Research and Development team drives innovation for GM customers. Specifically, the team works on advancing battery materials and systems, energy and propulsion systems, materials and manufacturing, connected vehicle tech, and software-defined technology. These innovations help create smarter, more efficient, and future-ready vehicles.

Yes, GM led the US. automotive industry in total, retail, and fleet sales for the first quarter of 2025, with 17% market share across its brands4.

GM vehicles are well-known for their long-lasting reliability, strong safety standards, and consistent performance. Since 1908, GM has prioritized excellence, reliability, and safety through rigorous testing and innovative engineering.

  2. GM Estimate based on total sales in 2024, comparison is year-over-year
  3. GM Estimate based on U.S. EV sales in 2025 Q1
  4. GM Estimate based on 2025 Q1 U.S. sales

DESIGN & ENGINEERING

Made to amaze

See our team in action

Redefining the drive

With a hunger for innovation, we are always putting our best ideas to the test and breaking boundaries to lead the industry forward. Each year, we invest an average of $7 billion in the U.S. on R&D because we believe in the creators, innovators, and dreamers driving change on a global scale.

Scroll to see our latest advancements in action.

Engineering the win

Racing is a sport decided in the details. It’s why we bring real-time data and AI together with precision engineering to create racecars that lead the pack.

Learn more

Driving a hands-free future

We’re bringing human ingenuity together with the latest advances in AI to push the frontiers of autonomous driving.

Learn more

Pioneering agility at every turn

We’re developing vehicles with features like CrabWalk1 and King Crab2 mode to move in any direction, ushering in a new era of off-road maneuverability long thought impossible.

Learn more

Excellence has a home

In locations across America, our expert teams help keep the engine of innovation running non-stop.

An expansive 710-acres dedicated to the art and science of design

Take a tour

We’re built for this

Designers, engineers, innovators. Our expert team of problem-solvers are the driving force behind GM’s exceptional portfolio of vehicles.

A century of innovation

1939
A roadmap to the future

In 1939, our visionary “Futurama” exhibit at the New York World’s Fair heavily influenced the development of the Interstate Highway System.

1955
Cure, accelerated

In 1955, we helped develop Centri-Filmer, a vaccine purifying machine that made large-scale manufacturing of the Salk polio vaccine possible.

1969
Becoming moonbound

In 1969, we helped NASA get the first humans to land on the moon with the Apollo 11 mission. We manufactured, tested, and integrated the inertial guidance and navigation system for the entire Apollo Moon program.

1997
Impact defined

In 1997, our Hybrid III crash test dummies were declared the official standard for frontal impact testing by the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

1977
An emissions breakthrough

In 1977, our experiments showed how unleaded gasoline would eliminate lead poisoning of the catalyst in vehicles. This led to us becoming the first automaker to offer cars that ran on unleaded gasoline, a major breakthrough in reducing vehicle exhaust emissions.

2011
Mission-critical robotics

In 2011, we partnered with NASA to create Robonaut 2, the first humanoid robot sent into space to assist astronauts as they work and explore.

2020
A COVID lifeline

In 2020, we mobilized our manufacturing ingenuity to produce and equip frontline healthcare professionals with lifesaving critical care ventilators.

CAREERS

Drive innovation with GM

If you’re an engineer or designer built to challenge the limits of automotive excellence, you’ve come to the right place.

Start your journey at GM

At GM, we thrive at the intersection of design and engineering, creating simplicity from complexity to make vehicles that customers are proud to own and love to drive. From becoming the first automotive manufacturer to standardize the automotive design process in product development to introducing innovations like Super Cruise hands-free driver assistance technology3 and Google Built-in4, we’ve always designed our vehicles with technical expertise to make driving smarter, safer, and more enjoyable.

For over a century, General Motors (GM) has been at the forefront of automotive engineering. From introducing the first mass-produced turbocharged car to pioneering the modern electric vehicle, electric pickup, and in-car touchscreen, GM has consistently led with bold ideas and real impact. We engineer the one for every drive and will continue to drive automotive innovation for generations to come. It’s part of our DNA.

GM’s design and engineering teams work together to blend creativity with technology. Concepts are developed, tested, and refined before being brought to life by manufacturing teams in state-of-the-art facilities.

GM’s new Design West facility, along with its predecessor, the Saarinen Building, are testaments to the creative forces that have defined GM’s design ethos since its founding. Design West’s large, open spaces allow for teams to congregate around the design process.

GM offers advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) like Super Cruise, which provide hands-free driver assistance3 on compatible roads but still require the driver to stay attentive. Super Cruise is powered by a Unified Lateral Controller — a self-learning, modular software system that uses real-time data and machine learning to manage lane centering, smooth lane changes, and adaptive steering.

https://www.gm.com/heritage.raw_html:
GM Heritage

Heritage of General Motors and its brands.

We are committed to preserving the rich history of General Motors brands while providing a foundation for continued innovation into the future.

Story of GM Founder, William Durant

The story of General Motors begins in Flint, Michigan, where, in 1886, William Crapo “Billy” Durant and Josiah Dallas Dort formed the Flint Road Cart Company and began building horse-drawn carriages. The company would become known as the Durant-Dort Carriage Company. It would grow to become one of the world’s largest carriage manufacturers, developing an international network of distributors and introducing such concepts as vertical integration and model differentiation to meet customer wants and need.

Durant was quiet and charismatic, earning a reputation as a super salesman and accomplished business leader. In 1904, he was asked to take over general management of the fledgling Buick Motor Co., which had been brought to Flint the year prior. Leveraging his knowledge, talents, and connections, in just four years, Durant developed Buick into the nation’s highest volume automobile producer in just four years.

Durant’s success with Buick led to the creation General Motors on September 16, 1908. Three years later, he founded Chevrolet, and grew it to a position of market leadership in just three short years. Durant left General Motors in early 1921, but his vision and ambition laid the groundwork for GM to become the largest industrial company in the world.

Learn More

The first 100 years of General Motors

Highlights from the GM Heritage Vehicle Collection

The GM Heritage Collection is made up of approximately 600 cars and trucks. Vehicles represented include GM industry firsts, significant technological experiments, concept cars, special-interest styling/performance one-offs along with notable race cars and milestone production vehicles. The GM Heritage Collection is ever-changing with new vehicles are constantly being obtained to fully represent GM's product story of the past 100+ years.

GM Heritage

The GM Heritage Archive includes over eight million photographic images, 250,000 video masters and motion picture films, a million and a half digital media files, and more than one million pieces of microfilm, available to the public upon request. Additionally, the Vehicle Information Kits allows you to search and download documents from over 900 models in the archive.

Explore more

GM Heritage Establishments

General Motors Factory One

The birthplace of General Motors, Factory One in Flint, Michigan, is available to the public for conference and event space. Ideal for community and education groups, vintage auto clubs, and historical organizations.

GM Heritage Center

Closed to the public at this time, the GM Heritage Center serves as a headquarters to the Heritage team and houses part of the GM Heritage Collection.

General Motors (GM) has a breadth of offerings that serve both consumers and businesses. GM’s family of vehicle brands — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac — ensures every driver can find the right vehicle. GM also offers a wide array of products to keep drivers on the road that span from automotive financing and software services to insurance and parts.

We build vehicles for every kind of driver and journey, including: electric, gas-powered, and vehicles with advanced driver assistance systems , as well as trucks, SUVs, sedans, coupes, hatchbacks, and commercial models. Whether you’re seeking power, efficiency, space, or style, we’re here to help you find the one for you. Explore our online breakdowns or visit a dealership to find the one for every drive.

GM has a longstanding history with motorsports. Currently, GM backs two racing teams: Chevrolet Motorsports and Cadillac Racing. The Cadillac Formula 1 team will join the 10 existing Formula 1 teams starting in 2026 through its partnership with TWG Motorsports. Winning on the racetrack is in our DNA – GM’s Chevy team has the most wins of any racing team in NASCAR with an impressive 102 NASCAR National Series wins at Dayton.
